questions.question: Which is the wrapper class for the primitive type char?
questions.explanation: Only int and char have wrapper names that differ from the primitive: Integer and Character.

questions.question: What does the compiler write for the line Integer fee = 49; ?
questions.explanation: Autoboxing is compiled to the wrapper's valueOf method, which can return a cached object.

questions.question: What does this print? Integer a = 128, b = 128; System.out.println(a == b);
questions.explanation: 128 is outside the Integer cache range of -128 to 127, so a and b are different objects and == compares references.

questions.question: What does this print? Integer a = 100, b = 100; System.out.println(a == b);
questions.explanation: 100 is inside the cached range, so both variables point to the same Integer object.

questions.question: Map<String, Integer> m = new HashMap<>(); int left = m.get("PLAN-9"); Why does this line crash?
options: The map returns null and unboxing calls intValue() on null
questions.explanation: get returns null for a missing key. Assigning it to an int unboxes it, which throws NullPointerException.

questions.question: What does this print? Long data = 3L; System.out.println(data.equals(3));
questions.explanation: 3 is boxed to an Integer. Long.equals returns false for any object that is not a Long.

questions.question: Why does Integer.parseInt("2GB") fail at run time?
options: parseInt only works on negative numbers
The text is not a valid integer, so it throws NumberFormatException
parseInt returns null for bad text
questions.explanation: parseInt accepts only an optional sign and digits. Strip the unit before parsing.

questions.question: What is the default value of an Integer field in a class, before it is assigned?
questions.explanation: Integer is an object type, so its field default is null. A primitive int field defaults to 0.

questions.question: What is the difference between Integer.parseInt("599") and Integer.valueOf("599")?
options: parseInt returns an int; valueOf returns an Integer object
parseInt returns an Integer; valueOf returns an int
Only valueOf can read negative numbers
There is no difference at all
questions.explanation: Both parse the same text. valueOf wraps the result in an Integer and may reuse a cached object.

questions.question: Long total = 0L; for (int i = 0; i < 1_000_000; i++) total += i; Why is this loop slow?
options: Each += unboxes, adds and boxes a new Long object
int and Long cannot be added
questions.explanation: The wrapper forces boxing on nearly every pass, creating many objects. A primitive long total avoids that.
